positive_controls.argument: Prospective value, remaining cost, opportunity cost and unavoidable obligations identify when intent should be reconsidered, retired or reduced rather than sustained by sunk effort.
The remaining decision value, investigation cost and option expiry identify when resolving the uncertainty is worth pursuing and when inquiry should stop or be narrowed.
Remaining value, cost, feasible alternatives and safe residual state supply a reasoned stop or redirect criterion before sunk design effort drives an unjustified commitment.
Prospective information and outcome value versus remaining cost provide a stopping criterion and prevent treating an accumulated prototype as a reason to continue.
The prospective-value and safe-exit comparison determines whether fit evidence supports continuing, narrowing, redirecting or retiring the product while honoring obligations.
Explicit prospective value, remaining cost, option expiry and safe residual obligations make stopping a real admissible option rather than a ceremonial threat.
Prospective value and remaining cost specify how to exercise the option at a stage boundary and when preserving it longer is itself wasteful.
Stopping and safe-residue criteria identify which workstream or increment can be retired and which dependent activities must finish or be reconfigured.
Prospective assurance value, continuing cost and safe residual obligations give a concrete basis for retiring redundant controls or retaining an adequate minimum.
The prospective stop or continue comparison identifies the decision-relevant horizon and opportunity cost, keeping sunk expense out of the remaining-value calculation.
The safe-exit state, remaining obligations and option expiry identify the consequences of withdrawal and the controls needed before the investment can be stopped.
